coverage_notes: Visually inspected all registered locations on PDF pp.14 and18, including both conflicting obs_002 presentations and the full Fig.13 pitting series. Table1 material composition p.3, sample preparation p.4 and test method/reference p.6 were viewed, along with title/context pp.1-2. Inputs and primary/secondary readings were preserved.
shared_qualifications: C20: Registered source potentials are already V on the SCE scale, so multiply by1000 to compare with CRA mV(SCE); no reference offset is applied.

Source conflict for obs_002: dedicated Table 3 and associated text (PDF p.14) give HEA/1M NaCl Epit -0.25 V(SCE), whereas Table 5 p.18 gives -0.49 V(SCE) for the same nominal condition. Both are retained; the source labels both SCE, so the 240 mV difference is not repaired by inventing an electrode conversion. CRA 585 agrees with the primary Table 3 reading but not the secondary Table 5 reading.

Method p.6 reports nitrogen deaeration, a1 mV/s sweep and three tests per condition. The tables do not supply individual replicate potentials or a statistical uncertainty for these outcomes; no replicates or means are manufactured.

For1M NaCl the method explicitly reports pH7.4, conflicting with CRA585 pH7.0. The0.1M pH is not explicitly supplied in the inspected passages; CRA584 pH7.0 is not treated as an independent source value.

Source Table 1 bulk composition is wt.%. Paper abstract/microstructure description calls the HEA almost amorphous with little BCC; the CSV description BCC with some amorphous structure reverses that emphasis. The original field remains unchanged and is not used to claim a verified phase fraction.

The registered sulfate-plus-chloride entries are explicitly pitting outcomes, but have no counterpart in the NaCl-only CSV. Their similar potentials do not make them equivalent to the1M NaCl result. Registered304S comparator observations also remain separate.
